newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil mulls kicking squatters out of gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Brazil mulls kicking squatters out of gold mine.

text.p: Brazil's government Monday held talks with officials from the Amazonian state of Para over a plan to evict hundreds of protesting wildcat miners from a huge gold deposit, officials said.
A Justice Ministry spokeswoman said Justice Minister Nelson Jobim went to Para state capital Belem to meet Para governor Almir Gabriel and that they would decide whether to send in the troops.

She denied that a decision was already made to clear protesters out from the area around the Serra Leste gold field, which has been blocked since May by up to 2,000 "garimpeiros", as freelance gold prospectors are called in Portuguese.

Newspapers reported Monday that the government was fed up with the garimpeiros stopping state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) from surveying the mine, which is thought to hold some 150 tonnes of gold.

The prospectors claim they are entitled to part of the gold in Serra Leste because it lies near Serra Pelada, site of the largest gold rush in history where up to one million garimpeiros produced 90 of the country's 113 tonnes of gold in 1988.
A CVRD spokesman said the company had not been informed of any government plan to send in the army or federal police to evict the protesting prospectors.
"We have had no information about this," he said.
He added that the number of squatters had declined since the protest started in May, and that of the 1,900 garimpeiros originally blocking the surveys, only about 450 were left.
CVRD estimates the garimpeiro protest has cost it at least $5.0 million. The spokesman said the mining giant had hoped to have advanced further in its surveys of Serra Leste.
